newsitem.title: UK: UK grain futures and cash markets in stalemate.
newsitem.headline: UK grain futures and cash markets in stalemate.

text.p: UK cash and futures market had reached stalemate on Friday with farmers not selling while traders wait for harvest pressure to force their hand.
"We have a situation now where old crop is around five stg less than new and people know that the farmers are going to have to sell soon, so why should they trade now?" said a broker.
Brokers said they foresee the market being stuck for the next two weeks.
"I can see farmers trying to hold out, but eventually the coming harvest will force them out," said another broker.
On the fob market prices were unchanged with no business reported while brokers reported only light trading mainly for nearby material on the delivered market where values were around 0.50 stg down.
One of the few trades reported was for harvest feed wheat in the Avon range at 87.50 stg a tonne.
LIFFE wheat futures closed with old crop 0.50 stg up and new crop 0.10 stg down to 0.40 stg higher on light turnover of 169 lots with most of the business coming in the last half an hour of trading.
LIFFE barley closed unchanged after trading 52 lots.
